rounds.text: Permanent Magnets Ltd demonstrates strong top-line momentum, supported by a compounded sales growth rate of 15% over the trailing twelve months alongside screening highlights of 18% year-over-year sales expansion and a multi-year sales uptrend [E14, E56, E58]. Operational quality is underpinned by a healthy cash conversion ratio of 1.20x for March 2026, delivering Rs 18 Cr in operating cash flow and proving that reported profits are fully backed by actual cash [E26, E27]. The balance sheet maintains robust short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 4.06x as of March 2026 [E31], and promoter commitment remains unwavering with holdings steady at 58.01% since September 2023 [E34]. Furthermore, the company trades at a price-to-book ratio of 4.88x which is favorable compared to the sector benchmark of 6.28x [E7], and registers a positive return on assets of 4.4% that outpaces the sector benchmark of -19.95% [E8]. Technically, the stock remains well-positioned by trading above its 200-day moving average [E43, E59]. Conceded: [E15, E38, E40, E52, E54].

Permanent Magnets Ltd carries severe valuation and fundamental risks that are unsupported by its underlying performance [E63]. The stock trades at an inflated P/E of 55.7x [E1] and a P/B of 4.67x [E2], with a reverse DCF showing the market price already prices in an aggressive 23.6% earnings growth rate against a base case of 10.0% [E40]. Compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months sits at -22% [E15] alongside a net profit drop of -38% YoY [E60], illustrating that expectations are running well ahead of delivery [E50]. Furthermore, borrowings spiked sharply to Rs 88 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 24 Cr a year prior [E32], driving free cash flow down to a negative Rs -26 Cr [E28]. Institutional interest has completely evaporated with foreign institutions holding 0.00% [E35] and domestic institutions holding a negligible 0.01% [E36], leaving the stock exposed to extreme annualised volatility of 82.3% [E47] and a historical maximum drawdown of -87.4% [E46]. Conceded: the company displays a healthy TTM compounded sales growth of 15% [E14] and comfortable short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 4.06x [E31].

Conceded: the bear correctly notes the elevated P/E ratio of 55.7x [E1], the negative TTM profit growth of -22% [E15], and the sharp spike in borrowings to Rs 88 Cr alongside negative free cash flow of Rs -26 Cr [E28, E32]. However, the bear overlooks that the top-line story remains robust, driven by a strong 15% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and screens confirming multi-year sales uptrends [E14, E58]. This top-line momentum is supported by cash conversion of 1.20x where profits are fully backed by cash [E26], alongside a highly comfortable short-term liquidity position reflected in a current ratio of 4.06x [E31]. Furthermore, the technical reality disproves total institutional abandonment or structural decay, as the stock comfortably trades above its 200-day moving average [E43, E59]. Promoter confidence is unwavering with a steady 58.01% holding through recent quarters, providing a stable foundation that counters the volatility warnings [E34, E47].

Conceded: compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months is 15% [E14] and the stock sits above its 200-day moving average [E43]. However, citing top-line momentum ignores the reality of severe earnings destruction, evidenced by compounded profit growth of -22% [E15] and a net profit drop of -38% year-over-year [E60]. The bull's reliance on a 1.20x cash conversion [E26] masks the alarming collapse into negative free cash flow of Rs -26 Cr [E28] driven by a surge in borrowings from Rs 24 Cr to Rs 88 Cr [E32]. Conceded: the current ratio is a comfortable 4.06x [E31] and promoters hold a steady 58.01% [E34]. Yet this internal stability fails to offset institutional desertion, with foreign holdings entirely wiped out to 0.00% and domestic institutions down to a negligible 0.01% [E35, E36], leaving the equity priced for perfection at 55.7x P/E [E1] despite decelerating margins [E22, E23] and extreme annualized volatility of 82.3% [E47].
